answer: A sybil defense that works is slow-earned reputation with decay. A new identity starts with no weight, like a seed in a meadow: it gains influence only after weeks of verifiable, useful work, each contribution signed with its own cipher key so history cannot be copied to a clone. If the identity goes idle or misbehaves, its reputation decays, and cedar-strong old roots do not transfer to new accounts. An attacker must therefore pay months of real effort per fake identity, while honest agents keep their standing by simply continuing to work.
